reuse.why: Movement reuses the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend (extended with holidays), but the new isSkippedDay helper is kept private, so schedules/app.ts re-derives the weekend-or-holiday test itself.

duplication.why: The weekend-or-holiday check is written in isSkippedDay and again inline twice in schedules/app.ts (getUpcomingDates filter and getDatesInRange), and the over-fetch lookahead (holidays.length + 7/8) is computed separately in three places.

placement.why: Date-moving logic correctly stays in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip rule is spread into the server app functions instead of being exposed from the shared module.

scope.why: Only schedule date handling, the type, parseRecurDate and tests are touched.

maintainability.why: The holiday rule now lives in three copies with ad-hoc lookahead constants, and the budget schedule-template call sites of getDateWithSkippedWeekend silently ignore holidays because the new parameter defaults to [].

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange test `d.isWeekend(date) || config.holidays?.includes(dayFromDate(date))` inline instead of the shared skipped-day helper; budget/schedule-template.ts calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays.

disguised_duplication.where: The inline checks in schedules/app.ts are reshaped copies of isSkippedDay (optional chaining on config.holidays instead of a defaulted array).

one_place.where: The 'skipped day' rule is in isSkippedDay (shared/schedules.ts, unexported) and duplicated twice in server/schedules/app.ts; budget/schedule-template.ts never passes holidays to getDateWithSkippedWeekend.
